content: {"experiments": [ [{"op": "put", "connection": "main", "key": "a", "value": 1}, {"op": "put", "connection": "main", "key": "a", "value": 2}], [{"op": "put", "connection": "main", "key": "a", "value": 1}, {"op": "update", "connection": "main", "key": "a", "value": 2}, {"op": "put", "connection": "main", "key": "a", "value": 3}], [{"op": "begin", "connection": "main", "key": null, "value": null}, {"op": "put", "connection": "main", "key": "a", "value": 1}, {"op": "put", "connection": "main", "key": "a", "value": 2}, {"op": "rollback", "connection": "main", "key": null, "value": null}, {"op": "put", "connection": "main", "key": "a", "value": 3}] ], "purpose": "Separate the three put conflict handlers and the channel definitions. Experiment 1: a duplicate-key put distinguishes INSERT OR IGNORE (no change, changes()=0) from INSERT OR REPLACE and ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE (one change each), and with the AFTER INSERT trigger reveals whether the trigger fires on the ignored insert. Experiment 2: put then update then put on the same key separates REPLACE (delete+insert, trigger fires on both puts) from DO UPDATE (update path, trigger fires only on the first put), and shows whether update counts in changes(). Experiment 3: a rolled-back transaction followed by a committed put tests whether changes()/total_changes count rolled-back direct changes (they do) versus committed effects, and whether the trigger's auxiliary log insert is counted by the channel, while committed_count/sum stay at one row."}
